title: Resolve the Phase 3 final review's confirmed findings
description:
Four findings from tick csr, all confirmed by the reviewer reading the code. Fix them in one pass; they are small and they cluster.

1. MEDIUM — A DECIDED DRAFT CAN STRAND FOREVER IN 'committing'.
cloud/factory/src/signal-inbox.ts:951, 988, 1090-1168. decide() sets state='committing' synchronously and THEN awaits #accept(), which calls commitTickRecord (a GitHub network call, up to 6 attempts with backoff). Both write-back paths — committed and unsettled — require #accept() to run to completion. If the DO is evicted mid-await (a wrangler deploy is enough), neither runs, and the row is left 'committing'. Every later decide() then returns already_decided, so the operator is told the proposal was handled when nothing was filed and nothing discarded — and they cannot tell whether GitHub accepted the write just before eviction.

The module's own eviction story covers submit() by arguing dedup makes a redelivery safe. That argument does not extend here: a human button press has no source that retries it.

Fix direction: a row found in 'committing' on a later invocation must be reconciled, not treated as decided — check whether the tick record actually exists and settle accordingly, or revert to pending so the button works again. Add the test that is missing: fail to run #accept() to completion and assert the draft is recoverable.

2. MEDIUM — TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_PATH is a duplicated literal.
cloud/factory/src/auth.ts:86 and cloud/factory/src/telegram.ts:95 each declare '/api/channels/telegram/webhook'. auth.ts decides which requests skip the bearer check with its copy; index.ts dispatches with the other. They agree today. Drift fails closed (the route would demand a token Telegram cannot send) so it is a maintenance hazard rather than a hole — but it is the duplicated-constant class .tick/learnings.md warns about, and tick spq's own report already flagged it. One shared constant.

3. LOW — fallbackBlock's external_ref bypasses the untrusted-text stripper.
cloud/factory/src/drafts.ts:147-154. escapeHTML only escapes & < > "; it does not strip control/bidi characters the way sanitizeUntrusted does. A generic source's external_ref is attacker-chosen (up to 512 chars) and fallbackBlock embeds it with escapeHTML alone — no line-break stripping, no '> ' quoting. A raw newline renders at column 0; a bidi override reorders what follows. NOT reachable today because both live sources always populate draft.presentation, so it is dead code — which is exactly why it should be fixed now rather than when a third source makes it live. Route it through the same sanitiser as everything else, and extend the forgery test to the fallback path.

4. LOW — draft to project binding is probabilistic, not structural.
cloud/factory/src/drafts.ts:93-99, 246-255. Callback data is d:<draft_id>:<verb> and does not name the project; findDraft iterates every enrolled project and takes the first inbox that answers. Draft ids are 48 random bits, unique only within one project's table. A collision would decide another project's draft silently. The odds are negligible and ids are not guessable — but the epic's own stated property is that an approval can never be attributed to the wrong project's gate, and here that rests on keyspace odds rather than on the callback naming the pair it decides. Put the project in the callback data and verify it matches; keep the payload inside Telegram's 64-byte callback_data limit.

closed_reason: Completed: all four confirmed findings from the Phase 3 final review. The stranded draft is the substantive one — decide() now treats a 'committing' row as a QUESTION rather than a decision, discriminating a live commit (this instance still working) from an evicted claim via an in-memory set, and answering the evicted case by asking whether the tick record actually exists rather than guessing. TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_PATH is now declared once; fallbackBlock routes external_ref through the same untrusted-text sanitiser as everything else; and callback data names a per-project handle so a draft decision can no longer resolve to another project's draft on an id collision.
